testParams.prompt: Using the information I have given you, please build a complete, simulatable quantitative stock-and-flow model of software project rework. Every stock must have a numeric initial value, every flow and auxiliary must have a well-defined equation, and the model must include simulation specifications (start time, stop time, time step, and time units) covering the full horizon described. The model must be able to run to completion in a system dynamics simulator without errors.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I want to understand why a software project takes longer than planned once undiscovered rework is taken into account.
additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: Model a fixed-scope software project with three stocks, all measured in tasks: work to be done, undiscovered rework, and work truly done. The team completes tasks at a work rate that flows out of work to be done. The work rate equals the number of developers times their productivity. A fraction of completed work is done correctly and flows into work truly done; the remaining fraction contains defects and flows into undiscovered rework instead. Undiscovered rework is not visible immediately: it is detected and flows back into work to be done at a rework discovery rate equal to the undiscovered rework stock divided by an average discovery delay. Use an initial work to be done of 500 tasks, an initial undiscovered rework of 0 tasks, and an initial work truly done of 0 tasks. Use 10 developers, a productivity of 0.4 tasks per developer per week, a fraction correct of 0.85 (so 0.15 of completed work becomes undiscovered rework), and an average discovery delay of 4 weeks. To avoid completed work continuing to be generated once the backlog is empty, the work rate should not exceed the amount of work remaining to be done. Simulate from week 0 to week 200 with a time step of 0.25 weeks, using weeks as the time unit.

expectations.problemStatement: I want to understand why a software project takes longer than planned once undiscovered rework is taken into account.

supportingInfo.explanation:
A quantitative stock-and-flow model of software project undiscovered rework has been built, configured, and validated.

Model Structure Overview

Stocks

  • work to be done: Initial value = 500 tasks (Units: tasks). Backlog of tasks waiting to be performed or reworked.
    • Inflow: rework discovery rate
    • Outflow: work rate
  • undiscovered rework: Initial value = 0 tasks (Units: tasks). Completed tasks that contain defects not yet detected.
    • Inflow: flawed work rate
    • Outflow: rework discovery rate
  • work truly done: Initial value = 0 tasks (Units: tasks). Cumulative tasks completed correctly without defect.
    • Inflow: correct work rate
    • Outflow: None

Parameters

  • developers: 10 (Units: developers)
  • productivity: 0.4 (Units: tasks/(developer*week))
  • fraction correct: 0.85 (Units: dimensionless)
  • average discovery delay: 4 (Units: weeks)

Flows and Auxiliary Variables

  • work rate: MIN(developers * productivity, work_to_be_done) (Units: tasks/week)
  • correct work rate: work_rate * fraction_correct (Units: tasks/week)
  • flawed work rate: work_rate * (1 - fraction_correct) (Units: tasks/week)
  • rework discovery rate: undiscovered_rework / average_discovery_delay (Units: tasks/week)

Simulation Specifications

  • Start Time: 0 weeks
  • Stop Time: 200 weeks
  • Time Step (dt): 0.25 weeks
  • Time Units: weeks
  • Integration Method: Euler

Validation and Simulation Check

The model was simulated successfully. The total task conservation identity (work to be done + undiscovered rework + work truly done = 500 tasks) holds across the entire 200-week time horizon, and non-negativity is preserved across all stocks.

What would you like to explore next? We can visualize time-series trajectories for the stocks and flows, conduct feedback loop dominance analysis, or perform policy and sensitivity experiments.

additionalParameters.problemStatement:
I've created this non-modular model simulating a predator-prey ecosystem.
            Please recreate the system with two modules.

            Use the following module names exactly:
            hare, lynx

            Component naming instructions:
            - Specifically rename "Hares" to "hare.hares", "area" to "hare.area", and "Lynx" to "lynx.lynx".
            - Otherwise, name components within each module by removing the animal prefix, and changing nothing else.
              For instance, 'hares killed per lynx' should be renamed to 'hare.killed_per_lynx', 
              and 'lynx births' should be renamed to 'lynx.births'.
            - Preserve the names of components that are not placed in modules.
            - When ghosting, preserve the original name of the ghosted component, including the module name if appropriate.
              For example, to create a ghost of "lynx.births" in the "hare" module, name the ghost component "hare.lynx births".
              To create a ghost of "lynx.lynx" in the "hare" module, name the ghost component "hare.lynx",
            Any other naming convention is unacceptable and will cause issues in my simulation.

            Try to preserve the key causal relationships and processes exactly, adding as few additional variables as possible
            and only when strictly necessary.

supportingInfo.explanation:
The predator-prey system model has been restructured into two distinct modules (hare and lynx) following the exact component and ghost naming conventions requested.

Model Architecture and Module Breakdown

1. hare Module

  • Stocks:
    • hare.hares: Initial population of $50{,}000\text{ hares}$. Inflow: hare.births, Outflow: hare.deaths.
  • Flows:
    • hare.births: Defined as $\text{hares} \times \text{birth_fraction}$ ($\text{hares/year}$).
    • hare.deaths: Defined as $\text{lynx} \times \text{killed_per_lynx}$ ($\text{hares/year}$).
  • Auxiliaries / Parameters:
    • hare.area: Habitat area defined as $1{,}000\text{ arce}$.
    • hare.density: Defined as $\text{hares} / \text{area}$ ($\text{hares/arce}$).
    • hare.birth_fraction: Fractional annual birth rate of $1.25\text{ 1/year}$.
    • hare.killed_per_lynx: Graphical lookup function taking density as input with points across the $[0, 500]$ range ($\text{hares/(lynx}\cdot\text{year)}$).
  • Ghost Variables:
    • hare.lynx: Cross-module ghost reference mirroring lynx.lynx from the lynx module.

2. lynx Module

  • Stocks:
    • lynx.lynx: Initial population of $850\text{ lynx}$ ($1{,}250 - 400$). Inflow: lynx.births, Outflow: lynx.deaths.
  • Flows:
    • lynx.births: Defined as $\text{lynx} \times \text{birth_fraction}$ ($\text{lynx/year}$).
    • lynx.deaths: Defined as $\text{lynx} \times \text{death_fraction}$ ($\text{lynx/year}$).
  • Auxiliaries / Parameters:
    • lynx.birth_fraction: Fractional annual birth rate of $0.25\text{ 1/year}$.
    • lynx.death_fraction: Graphical lookup function taking hare_density as input across the $[0, 100]$ range ($\text{1/year}$).
  • Ghost Variables:
    • lynx.hare_density: Cross-module ghost reference mirroring hare.density from the hare module.

Verification and Structural Integrity

  • Module Structure: Both modules (hare and lynx) are defined at the root level.
  • Ghost Aliases: Cross-module dependencies are connected via hare.lynx and lynx.hare_density.
  • Equations and Dimensions: Equations use module-local scope, graphical functions are populated, and all stock-flow relationships are connected without errors or engine warnings.

What would you like to do next with this modular model?

supportingInfo.explanation:
Overview of Changes and Rationale

The predator-prey system has been restructured from its original modular representation into a unified, non-modular Stock and Flow Diagram (SFD).

  1. Namespace Flattening & Component Naming:

    • Module prefixes (Hares. and Lynx.) were removed strictly according to the required specification (e.g., Hares.hare_density became hare_density, Lynx.lynx_births became lynx_births).
    • Cross-module ghost variables (Hares.Lynx and Lynx.hare_density) were removed because direct causal references are now established within a single shared namespace.

  2. Preservation of Equations & Lookups:

    • Stocks: Hares (initial value 50,000 hares) and Lynx (initial value 850 lynx).
    • Flows:
      • hare_births = Hares * hare_birth_fraction
      • hare_deaths = Lynx * hares_killed_per_lynx
      • lynx_births = Lynx * lynx_birth_fraction
      • lynx_deaths = Lynx * lynx_death_fraction
    • Auxiliary Variables & Lookups:
      • area = 1000
      • hare_birth_fraction = 1.25
      • hare_density = Hares / area
      • hares_killed_per_lynx = graphical function lookup of hare_density
      • lynx_birth_fraction = 0.25
      • lynx_death_fraction = non-linear lookup of hare_density (mortality starvation curve)

  3. Causal Structure & Integration:

    • The direct causal link from Lynx and hares_killed_per_lynx to hare_deaths replaces the previous cross-module ghost routing.
    • The link from hare_density to lynx_death_fraction replaces the corresponding cross-level ghost interface.

Model Structure Summary

  • Stocks (2): Hares, Lynx
  • Flows (4): hare_births, hare_deaths, lynx_births, lynx_deaths
  • Auxiliary Variables (6): area, hare_birth_fraction, hare_density, hares_killed_per_lynx, lynx_birth_fraction, lynx_death_fraction
  • Simulation Parameters: startTime = 0, stopTime = 100, dt = 0.03125 years, integration method = Euler.

Simulation & Verification

The unmodularized model was simulated across a 100-year time horizon in run eval-run-2:

  • Both populations demonstrate characteristic Lotka-Volterra oscillatory dynamics with lagging predator peaks following prey population expansions.
  • Hare population ranges between approximately 13,500 and 173,500 individuals.
  • Lynx population fluctuates between approximately 725 and 1,880 individuals.
  • Mass conservation and non-negativity constraints are fully satisfied across all time steps without artificial bounding clamps.

Next Steps

Would you like to:

  1. Visualize the time series of Hares and Lynx or generate a phase portrait (state-space plot)?
  2. Conduct parameter sensitivity analysis on predator hunting efficiency or prey natality rates?
  3. Test policy interventions, such as habitat area changes or harvesting scenarios?

            Any other naming convention is unacceptable and will cause issues in my simulation.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Actions Taken

  1. Model De-modularization: Converted the modular model into a single-level Stock-Flow Diagram (SFD) containing no module boundaries or namespaces.
  2. Component Renaming: Stripped all module prefixes (Population., Housing., Commerce.) from component names while retaining the exact original identifier names and specifications.
  3. Ghost Variable Elimination: Removed cross-level ghost variables (Population.Housing_Stock, Population.total_jobs, Housing.Population, Commerce.Population) that existed purely to support modular encapsulation, connecting their dependent formulations directly to the underlying model variables.
  4. Structural Verification: Preserved all original mathematical equations, safe division operators (//), graphical lookup tables, initial values, and dimensional units across all 31 components (3 stocks, 7 flows, and 21 auxiliary variables).

Non-Modular Model Structure

1. Stocks (Accumulations)

  • Population (Initial: 10,000 people)
    • Inflows: births, migration
    • Outflows: deaths
  • Housing_Stock (Initial: 4,000 units)
    • Inflows: construction
    • Outflows: demolition
  • Business_Structures (Initial: 500 structures)
    • Inflows: business_starts
    • Outflows: business_closures

2. Flows (Rates)

  • births = Population * birth_fraction (people/years)
  • deaths = Population * death_fraction (people/years)
  • migration = Population * base_migration_fraction * ((attractiveness_from_housing + attractiveness_from_jobs) / 2) (people/years)
  • construction = Housing_Stock * base_construction_fraction * construction_multiplier (units/years)
  • demolition = Housing_Stock * demolition_fraction (units/years)
  • business_starts = Business_Structures * base_start_fraction * start_multiplier (structures/years)
  • business_closures = Business_Structures * closure_fraction (structures/years)

3. Auxiliary Variables, Parameters, and Graphical Functions

  • Demographics:

    • birth_fraction = 0.02 (1/year)
    • death_fraction = 0.015 (1/year)
    • base_migration_fraction = 0.01 (1/year)
    • target_housing_per_person = 0.4 (units/person)
    • target_jobs_per_person = 1 (jobs/person)
    • relative_housing_availability = (Housing_Stock / Population) // target_housing_per_person (dimensionless)
    • relative_job_availability = (total_jobs / Population) // target_jobs_per_person (dimensionless)
    • attractiveness_from_housing = Graphical lookup on relative_housing_availability with points [(0, 0), (0.5, 0.5), (1, 1), (1.5, 1.3), (2, 1.5)] (dimensionless)
    • attractiveness_from_jobs = Graphical lookup on relative_job_availability with points [(0, 0), (0.5, 0.5), (1, 1), (1.5, 1.3), (2, 1.5)] (dimensionless)

  • Housing Sector:

    • base_construction_fraction = 0.05 (1/year)
    • demolition_fraction = 0.02 (1/year)
    • target_persons_per_house = 2.5 (people/unit)
    • relative_housing_demand = (Population / Housing_Stock) // target_persons_per_house (dimensionless)
    • construction_multiplier = Graphical lookup on relative_housing_demand with points [(0, 0), (0.5, 0.2), (1, 1), (1.5, 2), (2, 3)] (dimensionless)

  • Commerce & Labor Sector:

    • base_start_fraction = 0.05 (1/year)
    • closure_fraction = 0.03 (1/year)
    • target_labor_per_business = 20 (people/structure)
    • relative_labor_availability = (Population / Business_Structures) // target_labor_per_business (dimensionless)
    • start_multiplier = Graphical lookup on relative_labor_availability with points [(0, 0), (0.5, 0.2), (1, 1), (1.5, 2), (2, 3)] (dimensionless)
    • jobs_per_structure = 20 (jobs/structure)
    • total_jobs = Business_Structures * jobs_per_structure (jobs)

Verification and Simulation Status

  • The flattened model has been validated without structural errors.
  • A 50-year test simulation run completed successfully.

Next Steps

Please indicate if you would like to run specific policy experiments, explore parameter sensitivity, or generate visualizations of key output trajectories.

additionalParameters.problemStatement:
I've created this modular model simulating a predator-prey ecosystem.
            Please add a third module called 'cougars', representing cougars.
            
            As an apex predator, cougars are not hunted by any animal, and hunt lynxes to survive. 
            Cougars do not have any direct interactions with hares.

            Use the following component names in each module where appropriate:
            [animals], 
            [animal] births, [animal] deaths, 
            [animals] killed per [animal], [animal] density,
            [animal] birth fraction, [animal] death fraction
            - Note: [animal] is either "hare", "lynx", or "cougar"
            - Note: [animals] is either "hares", "lynx", or "cougars" (note the plural of "lynx" is "lynx")
            
            When ghosting, preserve the same variable name as in the source module. For instance, a ghost of "Hares.Hares"
            should be named "Lynx.Hares" in the "Lynx" module.

            You may add any necessary components, using appropriate names (as listed above) whenever possible.
            Do not modify or remove any existing causal relationships between lynxes and hares.

supportingInfo.explanation:
I have updated the model to include the third trophic module representing cougars and established the appropriate cross-module connections with the lynx population.

Structure of the Updated Model

  1. cougars Module:

    • Stock: cougars.cougars (initial population: 20 cougars)
    • Inflow: cougars.cougar_births (equation: cougars * cougar_birth_fraction)
    • Outflow: cougars.cougar_deaths (equation: cougars * cougar_death_fraction)
    • Variables:
      • cougars.cougar_birth_fraction: Annual natality fraction
      • cougars.cougar_death_fraction: Starvation mortality fraction determined by prey availability (lynx_density)
      • cougars.lynx_density: Cross-level ghost of Lynx.lynx_density

  2. Lynx Module Updates:

    • Stock: Lynx.Lynx
    • Inflow: Lynx.lynx_births
    • Outflow: Lynx.lynx_deaths (equation updated to: Lynx * lynx_death_fraction + cougars * lynx_killed_per_cougar)
    • Variables & Ghosts Added:
      • Lynx.lynx_density: Calculated as Lynx / area
      • Lynx.lynx_killed_per_cougar: Predation kill rate per cougar based on lynx density
      • Lynx.area: Cross-level ghost of Hares.area
      • Lynx.cougars: Cross-level ghost of cougars.cougars

  3. Hares Module:

    • Unchanged, preserving all existing formulations and relationships with lynx.
    • Cougars have no direct interaction with hares.

  4. Module Registry & Cross-Level Ghosts:

    • Registered modules: Hares, Lynx, cougars
    • Variable naming across module boundaries strictly preserves source variable base names in ghost variables (Lynx.cougars for cougars.cougars, cougars.lynx_density for Lynx.lynx_density, Lynx.area for Hares.area).

I've created this modular model simulating the urban dynamics in a city.

supportingInfo.explanation:
The Commerce module and all associated commercial and employment structures have been removed from the model. The remaining modular structure comprises the Population and Housing modules, coupled through residential availability and demand.

Summary of Modifications

  1. Commerce Module Removal:

    • Removed the commercial stock Commerce.Business_Structures.
    • Removed commercial flows: Commerce.business_starts and Commerce.business_closures.
    • Removed auxiliary variables and parameters: Commerce.base_start_fraction, Commerce.closure_fraction, Commerce.target_labor_per_business, Commerce.relative_labor_availability, Commerce.start_multiplier, Commerce.jobs_per_structure, Commerce.total_jobs, and the cross-level ghost Commerce.Population.

  2. Population Module Adjustments:

    • Removed employment-related ghost and auxiliary variables: Population.total_jobs, Population.target_jobs_per_person, Population.relative_job_availability, and Population.attractiveness_from_jobs.
    • Updated Population.migration to depend exclusively on baseline migration and housing attractiveness: Population * base_migration_fraction * attractiveness_from_housing

  3. Preserved Modules:

    • Population Module:
      • Stock: Population (Initial value: 10,000 people)
      • Inflows: births, migration
      • Outflow: deaths
      • Auxiliaries and Constants: birth_fraction (0.02 1/year), death_fraction (0.015 1/year), base_migration_fraction (0.01 1/year), target_housing_per_person (0.4 units/person), relative_housing_availability, attractiveness_from_housing (graphical lookup)
      • Ghost Variable: Housing_Stock (referencing Housing.Housing_Stock)
    • Housing Module:
      • Stock: Housing_Stock (Initial value: 4,000 units)
      • Inflow: construction
      • Outflow: demolition
      • Auxiliaries and Constants: base_construction_fraction (0.05 1/year), demolition_fraction (0.02 1/year), target_persons_per_house (2.5 people/unit), relative_housing_demand, construction_multiplier (graphical lookup)
      • Ghost Variable: Population (referencing Population.Population)

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Architecture and Formulation

A quantitative Stock-Flow Diagram (SFD) model has been constructed representing the three-role organizational hierarchy (aging chain) without modules.

1. State Variables (Stocks)

  • rookies (Initial value: 100 people)
    • Inflows: rookie_hires
    • Outflows: rookie_promotions, rookie_departures
    • Dynamic: Accumulation of entry-level rookie employees.
  • associates (Initial value: 50 people)
    • Inflows: rookie_promotions
    • Outflows: associate_promotions, associate_departures
    • Dynamic: Accumulation of mid-level associate employees.
  • partners (Initial value: 20 people)
    • Inflows: associate_promotions
    • Outflows: partner_departures
    • Dynamic: Accumulation of senior partner employees.

2. Rate Variables (Flows)

  • rookie_hires = hire_rate (Units: people/year, Uniflow: true)
  • rookie_promotions = rookies * promotion_rate (Units: people/year, Uniflow: true)
  • associate_promotions = associates * promotion_rate (Units: people/year, Uniflow: true)
  • rookie_departures = rookies * departure_rate (Units: people/year, Uniflow: true)
  • associate_departures = associates * departure_rate (Units: people/year, Uniflow: true)
  • partner_departures = partners * departure_rate (Units: people/year, Uniflow: true)

3. Parameters and Auxiliaries

  • hire_rate = 20 people/year
  • promotion_rate = 0.15 1/year
  • departure_rate = 0.05 1/year

Structural and Behavioral Validation

  • Dimensional Consistency: All units are strictly balanced across stocks (people), flows (people/year), and fractional rate constants (1/year). The engine reports zero unit warnings or errors.
  • Non-Negativity Control: All outflows are formulated with first-order linear feedback on their respective upstream stocks, precluding stocks from draining below zero under all operational conditions.
  • Simulation Verification: Baseline execution (eval-run-1) completed across a 50-year time horizon using Euler integration with dt = 0.25 years. The system demonstrates stable convergence toward steady-state distributions without numerical oscillation or non-conserved leakage.

Suggested Next Steps

We can visualize time-series trajectories for rookies, associates, and partners, conduct parameter sensitivity analysis on promotion_rate and departure_rate, or explore specific staffing policy scenarios.

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge:
Please rely on the following expert knowledge as much as possible when creating your model.


            In a certain city, a population depends on a nonrenewable resource.
            The population reproduces and dies off at steady rates proportional to the total population.
            The resource starts with a large initial quantity, but cannot be refilled.
            Over time, the resource diminishes at a rate proportional to the population.
            Define the "resource density" as the ratio of resource quantity to the population.
            If the resource density drops below a fixed threshold, then members of the population migrate away at
            a rate proportional to the total population and the difference between the resource density 
            and the minimum threshold.

            Please create a model with two modules, 'population' and 'resource'.

            Use the following component names within each module as appropriate:
            count, birth rate, births, death rate, deaths, usage rate, usage, density, density threshold, migrations

            All "rate" variables should be constant percentages.
            Please compute the resource density inside the 'resource' module, not the 'population' module.
            (The resource density threshold should be in the 'population' module, however.)
            Do not create any intermediate variables when calculating population migrations.

            When creating a ghost component, preserve the name of the original component, including the module prefix (separated by a space rather than a period).
            So, a ghost of "module1.component" in module2 should be named "module2.module1 component".

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Architecture and Formulation

A quantitative Stock Flow Diagram (SFD) model has been constructed with two modules: population and resource.

Module 1: population

  1. population.count (Stock)

    • Initial value: 1000 people
    • Inflows: population.births
    • Outflows: population.deaths, population.migrations
    • Units: people
    • Documentation: Total population residing in the city.

  2. population.birth rate (Variable)

    • Equation: 0.04
    • Units: 1/year
    • Documentation: Constant fractional annual birth rate.

  3. population.births (Flow)

    • Equation: population.count * population.birth_rate
    • Units: people/year
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Annual number of births entering the population stock.

  4. population.death rate (Variable)

    • Equation: 0.02
    • Units: 1/year
    • Documentation: Constant fractional annual baseline death rate.

  5. population.deaths (Flow)

    • Equation: population.count * population.death_rate
    • Units: people/year
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Annual number of baseline deaths leaving the population stock.

  6. population.density threshold (Variable)

    • Equation: 10
    • Units: units/person
    • Documentation: Minimum per-capita resource availability threshold below which out-migration is triggered.

  7. population.resource density (Ghost Variable)

    • Cross-level ghost of: resource.density
    • Units: units/person
    • Documentation: Ghost representation of resource density calculated in the resource module.

  8. population.migrations (Flow)

    • Equation: MAX(0, population.density_threshold - population.resource_density) * population.count
    • Units: people/year
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Direct out-migration rate triggered when resource density drops below the threshold, without intermediate variables.

Module 2: resource

  1. resource.count (Stock)

    • Initial value: 100000 units
    • Inflows: (none, nonrenewable resource)
    • Outflows: resource.usage
    • Units: units
    • Documentation: Total remaining stock of the nonrenewable resource.

  2. resource.usage rate (Variable)

    • Equation: 1.0
    • Units: units/(person*year)
    • Documentation: Constant per-capita consumption rate of the nonrenewable resource.

  3. resource.population count (Ghost Variable)

    • Cross-level ghost of: population.count
    • Units: people
    • Documentation: Ghost representation of the population stock from the population module.

  4. resource.usage (Flow)

    • Equation: resource.usage_rate * resource.population_count
    • Units: units/year
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Aggregate annual depletion rate of the nonrenewable resource driven by population demand.

  5. resource.density (Variable)

    • Equation: resource.count / resource.population_count
    • Units: units/person
    • Documentation: Per-capita resource density calculated directly within the resource module.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Thinking

The corporate hierarchy represents an aging chain structure where personnel advance through distinct professional stages (rookies, associates, and partners). To accurately capture this workflow, the model is decomposed into three separate modules representing each tier:

  • The rookies module accumulates new hires through a constant hiring flow and distributes outflows into departures and promotions based on fractional rates.
  • The associates module receives the promoted personnel from the rookie stage via a cross-level ghost interface (associates.rookies promotions), and drains through associate-level departures and promotions to partner.
  • The partners module receives promoted associates via its ghost interface (partners.associates promotions) and models partner departures.

Actions

  1. Generated the quantitative multi-module Stock Flow Diagram using generate_quantitative_model.
  2. Configured three distinct modules: rookies, associates, and partners.
  3. Established stocks, inflows, outflows, auxiliary variables, and cross-module ghost linkages according to specified naming rules:
    • Module rookies:
      • Stock: rookies.count [people]
      • Inflow: rookies.hires [people/year] (governed by rookies.hire_rate = 20 people/year)
      • Outflow: rookies.departures [people/year] (governed by rookies.departure_rate = 0.1 1/year)
      • Outflow: rookies.promotions [people/year] (governed by rookies.promotion_rate = 0.2 1/year)
    • Module associates:
      • Stock: associates.count [people]
      • Ghost variable: associates.rookies promotions mirroring rookies.promotions
      • Inflow: associates.hires [people/year] (driven by associates.rookies_promotions)
      • Outflow: associates.departures [people/year] (governed by associates.departure_rate = 0.05 1/year)
      • Outflow: associates.promotions [people/year] (governed by associates.promotion_rate = 0.1 1/year)
    • Module partners:
      • Stock: partners.count [people]
      • Ghost variable: partners.associates promotions mirroring associates.promotions
      • Inflow: partners.hires [people/year] (driven by partners.associates_promotions)
      • Outflow: partners.departures [people/year] (governed by partners.departure_rate = 0.05 1/year)
  4. Validated the complete module hierarchy, variable definitions, and causal relationship polarities.

Results

The model structure contains:

  • 3 modules: rookies, associates, partners
  • 3 stocks: rookies.count, associates.count, partners.count
  • 7 flows: rookies.hires, rookies.departures, rookies.promotions, associates.hires, associates.departures, associates.promotions, partners.hires, partners.departures
  • 7 auxiliary parameters: rookies.hire_rate, rookies.departure_rate, rookies.promotion_rate, associates.departure_rate, associates.promotion_rate, partners.departure_rate
  • 2 cross-level ghost variables linking promotion outflows to subsequent tier hiring inflows: associates.rookies promotions and partners.associates promotions
  • Consistent unit specifications throughout all equations.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to understand the key causal mechanisms that drive this system's behavior over time.
additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge:
Please rely on the following expert knowledge as much as possible when creating your model.


            In a certain ecosystem, there are three animal populations: lions, foxes, and chickens.
            
            All species reproduce and naturally die out at specific, stable percentage rates.
            Furthermore, the chicken population is predated at a rate proportional to the fox population,
            and the fox population is predated at a rate proportional to the lion population.
            
            Create a model with three modules named 'lions', 'foxes', and 'chickens'.
            
            Use the following component names within each module as appropriate:
            count, birth rate, death rate, births, deaths, predation rate

            In particular, "[animal].predation rate" should refer to the number of [animal]s that die off due to that animal's predator.

            When creating a ghost component, preserve the name of the original component, including the module prefix (separated by a space rather than a period).
            So, a ghost of "module1.component" in module2 should be named "module2.module1 component".

supportingInfo.explanation:
A quantitative Stock Flow Diagram (SFD) model has been constructed according to the exact specifications and modular architecture requested.

Model Architecture

The model is partitioned into three distinct modules: lions, foxes, and chickens.

1. lions Module

Apex predator population module:

  • Stock: lions.count (Initial value: 10 lions)
    • Inflows: lions.births
    • Outflows: lions.deaths
  • Variables:
    • lions.birth rate: 0.1 (1/year)
    • lions.death rate: 0.08 (1/year)
  • Flows:
    • lions.births: lions.count * lions.birth_rate (lions/year)
    • lions.deaths: lions.count * lions.death_rate (lions/year)

2. foxes Module

Mesopredator population module:

  • Stock: foxes.count (Initial value: 50 foxes)
    • Inflows: foxes.births
    • Outflows: foxes.deaths, foxes.predation rate
  • Variables:
    • foxes.birth rate: 0.25 (1/year)
    • foxes.death rate: 0.1 (1/year)
    • foxes.lions count: Ghost variable of lions.count
  • Flows:
    • foxes.births: foxes.count * foxes.birth_rate (foxes/year)
    • foxes.deaths: foxes.count * foxes.death_rate (foxes/year)
    • foxes.predation rate: foxes.lions_count (foxes/year)

3. chickens Module

Prey population module:

  • Stock: chickens.count (Initial value: 500 chickens)
    • Inflows: chickens.births
    • Outflows: chickens.deaths, chickens.predation rate
  • Variables:
    • chickens.birth rate: 0.5 (1/year)
    • chickens.death rate: 0.15 (1/year)
    • chickens.foxes count: Ghost variable of foxes.count
  • Flows:
    • chickens.births: chickens.count * chickens.birth_rate (chickens/year)
    • chickens.deaths: chickens.count * chickens.death_rate (chickens/year)
    • chickens.predation rate: chickens.foxes_count (chickens/year)

Simulation Specifications

  • Time Horizon: 0 to 50
  • Time Step (dt): 0.25
  • Time Units: Years
  • Integration Method: Euler

supportingInfo.explanation:
A quantitative System Dynamics model has been constructed to capture the causal structure and quantitative relationships described in the background information.

Model Architecture and Components

The model is organized into two distinct modules corresponding to each object:

1. Module: whatajigs

  • Stock:
    • whatajigs.count: Initialized at 100 whatajigs. Represents the inventory quantity of whatajigs over time.
  • Inflow:
    • whatajigs.growth: Rate of incoming growth, calculated as whatajigs.count * whatajigs.growth_fraction (units: whatajigs/years).
  • Outflow:
    • whatajigs.diminishing: Rate of inventory reduction, calculated as whatajigs.balacks_count * whatajigs.diminishing_rate (units: whatajigs/years).
  • Auxiliary Variables & Parameters:
    • whatajigs.growth_fraction: Parameter set to 0.05 (units: 1/years), representing the 5% annual growth rate relative to current whatajig inventory.
    • whatajigs.diminishing_rate: Parameter set to 3.0 (units: whatajigs/(balacks*years)), representing the 300% annual diminishing multiplier per available balack.
  • Ghost Variable:
    • whatajigs.balacks count: Cross-level ghost importing balacks.count from the balacks module into the whatajigs module.

2. Module: balacks

  • Stock:
    • balacks.count: Initialized at 200 balacks. Represents the inventory quantity of balacks over time.
  • Inflow:
    • balacks.increase: Rate of incoming balacks, calculated as balacks.whatajigs_count * balacks.increase_rate (units: balacks/years).
  • Outflow:
    • balacks.outgoing: Rate of outgoing balacks, calculated as balacks.count * balacks.outgoing_fraction (units: balacks/years).
  • Auxiliary Variables & Parameters:
    • balacks.increase_rate: Parameter set to 0.05 (units: balacks/(whatajigs*years)), representing the 5% annual addition driven by the whatajigs count.
    • balacks.outgoing_fraction: Parameter set to 0.03 (units: 1/years), representing the 3% annual outgoing rate of current balacks inventory.
  • Ghost Variable:
    • balacks.whatajigs count: Cross-level ghost importing whatajigs.count from the whatajigs module into the balacks module.

Direct Causal Relationships

  • whatajigs.count -> whatajigs.growth (+)
  • whatajigs.growth_fraction -> whatajigs.growth (+)
  • whatajigs.growth -> whatajigs.count (+)
  • whatajigs.balacks count -> whatajigs.diminishing (+)
  • whatajigs.diminishing_rate -> whatajigs.diminishing (+)
  • whatajigs.diminishing -> whatajigs.count (-)
  • balacks.whatajigs count -> balacks.increase (+)
  • balacks.increase_rate -> balacks.increase (+)
  • balacks.increase -> balacks.count (+)
  • balacks.count -> balacks.outgoing (+)
  • balacks.outgoing_fraction -> balacks.outgoing (+)
  • balacks.outgoing -> balacks.count (-)

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: Throughout the process, we have on hand fifty marticatenes. Every month, this inventory is enhanced by exactly ten new marticatenes. Simultaneously, each month the stock decreases by 20% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, there are initially seventy-five refluppers. Every month, this inventory gains from 20% of the current marticatenes count. Simultaneously, each month the stock gets diminished by a constant eight refluppers.  Meanwhile, our records indicate one hundred twenty exemintes. Every month, this inventory grows through incoming exactly eight new exemintes. Simultaneously, each month the stock is reduced through 10% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
A modular Stock Flow Diagram (SFD) model has been constructed to represent all entities, accumulations, flows, and causal dependencies specified in the background information.

Model Architecture and Modular Structure

The model is organized into three distinct top-level modules corresponding to the three object types:

1. Module marticatenes

  • Stock marticatenes.count: Holds the current inventory of marticatenes.
    • Initial Value: 50 marticatenes
    • Inflows: marticatenes.enhancement
    • Outflows: marticatenes.decrease
    • Units: marticatenes
  • Flow marticatenes.enhancement: Rate of incoming new marticatenes added to inventory each month.
    • Equation: marticatenes.enhancement_rate
    • Units: marticatenes/Months
  • Variable marticatenes.enhancement_rate: Constant monthly enhancement amount.
    • Equation: 10
    • Units: marticatenes/Months
  • Flow marticatenes.decrease: Monthly outflow draining marticatenes inventory proportionally.
    • Equation: marticatenes.count * marticatenes.fractional_decrease_rate
    • Units: marticatenes/Months
  • Variable marticatenes.fractional_decrease_rate: Monthly fractional decrease rate.
    • Equation: 0.2
    • Units: 1/Months

2. Module refluppers

  • Stock refluppers.count: Holds the current inventory of refluppers.
    • Initial Value: 75 refluppers
    • Inflows: refluppers.gain
    • Outflows: refluppers.diminishment
    • Units: refluppers
  • Ghost Variable refluppers.marticatenes count: Cross-module reference bringing marticatenes.count into the refluppers module.
    • Source: marticatenes.count
    • Units: marticatenes
  • Flow refluppers.gain: Inflow generated monthly as a fraction of the current marticatenes inventory.
    • Equation: refluppers.marticatenes_count * refluppers.fractional_gain_rate
    • Units: refluppers/Months
  • Variable refluppers.fractional_gain_rate: Rate multiplier determining the refluppers gain per marticatene per month.
    • Equation: 0.2
    • Units: refluppers/(marticatenes*Months)
  • Flow refluppers.diminishment: Constant monthly outflow reducing refluppers.
    • Equation: refluppers.diminishing_rate
    • Units: refluppers/Months
  • Variable refluppers.diminishing_rate: Constant rate of refluppers diminishment.
    • Equation: 8
    • Units: refluppers/Months

3. Module exemintes

  • Stock exemintes.count: Holds the current inventory of exemintes.
    • Initial Value: 120 exemintes
    • Inflows: exemintes.growth
    • Outflows: exemintes.reduction
    • Units: exemintes
  • Flow exemintes.growth: Inflow adding incoming exemintes each month.
    • Equation: exemintes.growth_rate
    • Units: exemintes/Months
  • Variable exemintes.growth_rate: Constant monthly incoming quantity.
    • Equation: 8
    • Units: exemintes/Months
  • Flow exemintes.reduction: Monthly outflow reducing exemintes inventory proportionally.
    • Equation: exemintes.count * exemintes.fractional_reduction_rate
    • Units: exemintes/Months
  • Variable exemintes.fractional_reduction_rate: Monthly fractional reduction rate.
    • Equation: 0.1
    • Units: 1/Months

Simulation Specifications

  • Start Time: 0 Months
  • Stop Time: 24 Months
  • Time Step (dt): 0.25 Months
  • Time Units: Months
  • Integration Method: Euler

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: In my business, our records indicate thirty-five povals. Every day, this inventory grows through incoming 30% of the current dominitoxings count. Simultaneously, each day the stock experiences losses of 20% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we start the period with ninety auspongs. Every day, this inventory increases due to 20% of the current povals count. Simultaneously, each day the stock suffers depletion of a constant twelve auspongs.  Meanwhile, we have on hand forty-five dominitoxings. Every day, this inventory increases due to exactly twelve new dominitoxings. Simultaneously, each day the stock experiences losses of 30% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Architecture and Causal Structure

A modular System Dynamics model has been constructed to represent the coupled inventory system for povals, auspongs, and dominitoxings.

1. Module Structure and Specifications

Simulation Specs:

  • Start Time: 0 days
  • Stop Time: 50 days
  • Time Step (dt): 0.25 days
  • Time Units: days
  • Integration Method: Euler

2. Module Details

Module 1: dominitoxings

  • Stock: dominitoxings.count

    • Initial Value: 45 dominitoxings
    • Inflow: dominitoxings.incoming dominitoxings
    • Outflow: dominitoxings.dominitoxing losses
    • Units: dominitoxings
    • Documentation: Accumulation of dominitoxings on hand.

  • Flow: dominitoxings.incoming dominitoxings

    • Equation: dominitoxings_inflow_rate
    • Units: dominitoxings/days
    • Documentation: Constant arrival of twelve new dominitoxings per day.

  • Flow: dominitoxings.dominitoxing losses

    • Equation: count * dominitoxings_loss_fraction
    • Units: dominitoxings/days
    • Documentation: Outflow depleting 30% of current dominitoxings count per day.

  • Parameter: dominitoxings.dominitoxings inflow rate

    • Equation: 12
    • Units: dominitoxings/days

  • Parameter: dominitoxings.dominitoxings loss fraction

    • Equation: 0.3
    • Units: 1/days

Module 2: povals

  • Stock: povals.count

    • Initial Value: 35 povals
    • Inflow: povals.incoming povals
    • Outflow: povals.poval losses
    • Units: povals
    • Documentation: Accumulation of povals in business inventory.

  • Ghost Variable: povals.dominitoxings count

    • Cross-Level Source: dominitoxings.count
    • Units: dominitoxings
    • Documentation: Cross-module ghost reference to dominitoxings.count.

  • Flow: povals.incoming povals

    • Equation: dominitoxings_count * poval_growth_fraction
    • Units: povals/days
    • Documentation: Inflow growing at 30% of current dominitoxings count per day.

  • Flow: povals.poval losses

    • Equation: count * poval_loss_fraction
    • Units: povals/days
    • Documentation: Proportional loss rate of 20% of current poval stock per day.

  • Parameter: povals.poval growth fraction

    • Equation: 0.3
    • Units: 1/days

  • Parameter: povals.poval loss fraction

    • Equation: 0.2
    • Units: 1/days

Module 3: auspongs

  • Stock: auspongs.count

    • Initial Value: 90 auspongs
    • Inflow: auspongs.incoming auspongs
    • Outflow: auspongs.auspong depletion
    • Units: auspongs
    • Documentation: Accumulation of auspongs in inventory over time.

  • Ghost Variable: auspongs.povals count

    • Cross-Level Source: povals.count
    • Units: povals
    • Documentation: Cross-module ghost reference to povals.count.

  • Flow: auspongs.incoming auspongs

    • Equation: povals_count * auspong_growth_fraction
    • Units: auspongs/days
    • Documentation: Daily inflow driven by 20% of the current povals count.

  • Flow: auspongs.auspong depletion

    • Equation: auspong_depletion_rate
    • Units: auspongs/days
    • Documentation: Constant depletion rate of twelve auspongs per day.

  • Parameter: auspongs.auspong growth fraction

    • Equation: 0.2
    • Units: 1/days

  • Parameter: auspongs.auspong depletion rate

    • Equation: 12
    • Units: auspongs/days

3. Causal Relationship Matrix

From Variable To Variable Polarity Causal Reasoning
dominitoxings.dominitoxings inflow rate dominitoxings.incoming dominitoxings + Higher inflow rate parameter increases incoming flow.
dominitoxings.incoming dominitoxings dominitoxings.count + Inflow increases total accumulated dominitoxings.
dominitoxings.count dominitoxings.dominitoxing losses + Higher stock level generates larger fractional losses.
dominitoxings.dominitoxings loss fraction dominitoxings.dominitoxing losses + Higher fractional loss rate increases total loss rate.
dominitoxings.dominitoxing losses dominitoxings.count - Outflow drains the dominitoxings stock.
povals.dominitoxings count povals.incoming povals + Higher dominitoxings stock drives a higher inflow of povals.
povals.poval growth fraction povals.incoming povals + Higher conversion multiplier increases poval arrival rate.
povals.incoming povals povals.count + Inflow accumulates into the poval inventory.
povals.count povals.poval losses + Larger stock size increases daily poval losses.
povals.poval loss fraction povals.poval losses + Greater loss fraction increases the poval outflow rate.
povals.poval losses povals.count - Loss outflow depletes the accumulated poval stock.
auspongs.povals count auspongs.incoming auspongs + More povals produce a higher incoming flow of auspongs.
auspongs.auspong growth fraction auspongs.incoming auspongs + Larger multiplier scales the rate of incoming auspongs.
auspongs.incoming auspongs auspongs.count + Inflow increases the total accumulated stock of auspongs.
auspongs.auspong depletion rate auspongs.auspong depletion + Higher depletion rate parameter increases outflow.
auspongs.auspong depletion auspongs.count - Depletion flow subtracts directly from the auspong inventory.

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: In my business, the baseline inventory shows one hundred ten pablanksills. Every quarter, this inventory benefits from 6% growth relative to its current size. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock gets diminished by a constant eighteen pablanksills.  Meanwhile, the baseline inventory shows seventy posistorathers. Every quarter, this inventory increases due to exactly twenty-five new posistorathers. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock suffers depletion of 35% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we start the period with ninety-five crypterals. Every quarter, this inventory receives new additions of exactly eighteen new crypterals. Every quarter, this inventory is enhanced by 35% of the current posistorathers count. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock decreases by 22% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Thinking

The goal is to structure a modular Stock and Flow model extracting all causal relationships from the provided business inventory description across three components: pablanksills, posistorathers, and crypterals.

  1. System Boundaries & Modularization:

    • Three distinct modules are defined: pablanksills, posistorathers, and crypterals.
    • Each module encapsulates its primary accumulation variable (count), inflows, outflows, and parameter variables.
    • Cross-module interaction from posistorathers.count to the crypterals module is represented via a ghost variable (crypterals.posistorathers count) referencing the source stock posistorathers.count.

  2. Formulation Details:

    • Module pablanksills:
      • Stock pablanksills.count initialized at 110 pablanksills.
      • Fractional growth parameter pablanksills.growth_fraction = 0.06 (1/quarter).
      • Inflow pablanksills.growth = count * growth_fraction.
      • Constant diminishing parameter pablanksills.diminishing_rate = 18 (pablanksills/quarter).
      • Outflow pablanksills.diminishing = diminishing_rate.
    • Module posistorathers:
      • Stock posistorathers.count initialized at 70 posistorathers.
      • Constant addition parameter posistorathers.addition_rate = 25 (posistorathers/quarter).
      • Inflow posistorathers.additions = addition_rate.
      • Proportional depletion parameter posistorathers.depletion_fraction = 0.35 (1/quarter).
      • Outflow posistorathers.depletion = count * depletion_fraction.
    • Module crypterals:
      • Stock crypterals.count initialized at 95 crypterals.
      • Constant addition parameter crypterals.addition_rate = 18 (crypterals/quarter).
      • Inflow crypterals.additions = addition_rate.
      • Cross-level ghost variable crypterals.posistorathers count referencing posistorathers.count.
      • Enhancement parameter crypterals.enhancement_fraction = 0.35 (1/quarter).
      • Cross-module inflow crypterals.enhancement = posistorathers_count * enhancement_fraction.
      • Proportional decrease parameter crypterals.decrease_fraction = 0.22 (1/quarter).
      • Outflow crypterals.decrease = count * decrease_fraction.

Actions

  • Generated and validated the modular Stock and Flow diagram across the three subsystems.
  • Configured explicit simulation specifications: startTime = 0, stopTime = 20, dt = 0.25, timeUnits = 'quarter', and integration method Euler.
  • Defined all 18 variables with non-embedded, fully abstracted parameters and assigned units and documentation.
  • Specified all 18 causal relationships with corresponding causal polarities.

Model Structure Summary

1. Module pablanksills

  • Stocks:
    • pablanksills.count (Initial Value: 110 pablanksills; Inflows: [pablanksills.growth], Outflows: [pablanksills.diminishing])
  • Flows:
    • pablanksills.growth = count * growth_fraction (Units: pablanksills/quarter)
    • pablanksills.diminishing = diminishing_rate (Units: pablanksills/quarter)
  • Parameters:
    • pablanksills.growth_fraction = 0.06 (Units: 1/quarter)
    • pablanksills.diminishing_rate = 18 (Units: pablanksills/quarter)
  • Causal Relationships:
    • pablanksills.count -> pablanksills.growth (+)
    • pablanksills.growth_fraction -> pablanksills.growth (+)
    • pablanksills.growth -> pablanksills.count (+)
    • pablanksills.diminishing_rate -> pablanksills.diminishing (+)
    • pablanksills.diminishing -> pablanksills.count (-)

2. Module posistorathers

  • Stocks:
    • posistorathers.count (Initial Value: 70 posistorathers; Inflows: [posistorathers.additions], Outflows: [posistorathers.depletion])
  • Flows:
    • posistorathers.additions = addition_rate (Units: posistorathers/quarter)
    • posistorathers.depletion = count * depletion_fraction (Units: posistorathers/quarter)
  • Parameters:
    • posistorathers.addition_rate = 25 (Units: posistorathers/quarter)
    • posistorathers.depletion_fraction = 0.35 (Units: 1/quarter)
  • Causal Relationships:
    • posistorathers.addition_rate -> posistorathers.additions (+)
    • posistorathers.additions -> posistorathers.count (+)
    • posistorathers.count -> posistorathers.depletion (+)
    • posistorathers.depletion_fraction -> posistorathers.depletion (+)
    • posistorathers.depletion -> posistorathers.count (-)

3. Module crypterals

  • Stocks:
    • crypterals.count (Initial Value: 95 crypterals; Inflows: [crypterals.additions, crypterals.enhancement], Outflows: [crypterals.decrease])
  • Flows:
    • crypterals.additions = addition_rate (Units: crypterals/quarter)
    • crypterals.enhancement = posistorathers_count * enhancement_fraction (Units: crypterals/quarter)
    • crypterals.decrease = count * decrease_fraction (Units: crypterals/quarter)
  • Parameters & Ghost Variables:
    • crypterals.addition_rate = 18 (Units: crypterals/quarter)
    • crypterals.posistorathers count (Ghost of posistorathers.count; Units: posistorathers)
    • crypterals.enhancement_fraction = 0.35 (Units: 1/quarter)
    • crypterals.decrease_fraction = 0.22 (Units: 1/quarter)
  • Causal Relationships:
    • crypterals.addition_rate -> crypterals.additions (+)
    • crypterals.additions -> crypterals.count (+)
    • crypterals.posistorathers count -> crypterals.enhancement (+)
    • crypterals.enhancement_fraction -> crypterals.enhancement (+)
    • crypterals.enhancement -> crypterals.count (+)
    • crypterals.count -> crypterals.decrease (+)
    • crypterals.decrease_fraction -> crypterals.decrease (+)
    • crypterals.decrease -> crypterals.count (-)

Next Steps

  • Perform baseline simulation runs over desired operational time horizons.
  • Run parameter sensitivity tests on fractional inflow and outflow rates across modules.

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: In my business, our records indicate twenty-five ocs. Every week, this inventory grows through incoming 15% of the current proptimatires count. Simultaneously, each week the stock suffers depletion of a constant three ocs.  Meanwhile, we have on hand forty proptimatires. Every week, this inventory gets replenished by exactly five new proptimatires. Simultaneously, each week the stock gets diminished by 25% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, there are initially eighty priaries. Every week, this inventory is enhanced by 10% of the current proptimatires count. Simultaneously, each week the stock decreases by 5% of whatever houtals are currently available.  Meanwhile, we have on hand sixty houtals. supportingInfo.explanation:
A fully specified Stock Flow Diagram model has been constructed with four modules corresponding to each component.

Model Architecture and Specifications

Simulation Specifications

  • Time Horizon: 0 to 50 weeks
  • Time Step (dt): 0.25 weeks
  • Time Units: weeks
  • Integration Method: Euler

Module Breakdown

1. Module: ocs

  • Stock: ocs.count
    • Initial Value: 25 ocs
    • Inflows: ocs.incoming
    • Outflows: ocs.depletion
    • Units: ocs
    • Documentation: Current stock accumulation of ocs inventory.
  • Inflow: ocs.incoming
    • Equation: growth_fraction * proptimatires_count
    • Units: ocs/weeks
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Weekly incoming flow of ocs driven by proptimatires count.
  • Outflow: ocs.depletion
    • Equation: depletion_rate
    • Units: ocs/weeks
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Weekly constant depletion rate of ocs.
  • Parameter: ocs.growth_fraction
    • Equation: 0.15
    • Units: 1/weeks
    • Documentation: Fractional weekly growth rate multiplier applied to proptimatires count.
  • Parameter: ocs.depletion_rate
    • Equation: 3
    • Units: ocs/weeks
    • Documentation: Constant weekly depletion rate of ocs.
  • Cross-Module Ghost: ocs.proptimatires count
    • Source: proptimatires.count
    • Units: proptimatires
    • Documentation: Cross-module ghost variable of proptimatires stock count.

2. Module: proptimatires

  • Stock: proptimatires.count
    • Initial Value: 40 proptimatires
    • Inflows: proptimatires.replenishment
    • Outflows: proptimatires.diminishment
    • Units: proptimatires
    • Documentation: Current stock accumulation of proptimatires.
  • Inflow: proptimatires.replenishment
    • Equation: replenishment_rate
    • Units: proptimatires/weeks
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Weekly replenishment inflow to proptimatires.
  • Outflow: proptimatires.diminishment
    • Equation: count * diminishment_fraction
    • Units: proptimatires/weeks
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Proportional draining outflow of proptimatires.
  • Parameter: proptimatires.replenishment_rate
    • Equation: 5
    • Units: proptimatires/weeks
    • Documentation: Constant weekly replenishment rate of proptimatires.
  • Parameter: proptimatires.diminishment_fraction
    • Equation: 0.25
    • Units: 1/weeks
    • Documentation: Fractional weekly diminishment rate of proptimatires.

3. Module: priaries

  • Stock: priaries.count
    • Initial Value: 80 priaries
    • Inflows: priaries.enhancement
    • Outflows: priaries.decrease
    • Units: priaries
    • Documentation: Current stock accumulation of priaries.
  • Inflow: priaries.enhancement
    • Equation: enhancement_fraction * proptimatires_count
    • Units: priaries/weeks
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Weekly enhancement inflow to priaries influenced by proptimatires count.
  • Outflow: priaries.decrease
    • Equation: decrease_fraction * houtals_count
    • Units: priaries/weeks
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Weekly decrease outflow from priaries influenced by houtals count.
  • Parameter: priaries.enhancement_fraction
    • Equation: 0.1
    • Units: 1/weeks
    • Documentation: Fractional weekly enhancement multiplier from proptimatires.
  • Parameter: priaries.decrease_fraction
    • Equation: 0.05
    • Units: 1/weeks
    • Documentation: Fractional weekly decrease multiplier from houtals.
  • Cross-Module Ghost: priaries.proptimatires count
    • Source: proptimatires.count
    • Units: proptimatires
    • Documentation: Cross-module ghost variable of proptimatires stock count in priaries module.
  • Cross-Module Ghost: priaries.houtals count
    • Source: houtals.count
    • Units: houtals
    • Documentation: Cross-module ghost variable of houtals stock count in priaries module.

4. Module: houtals

  • Stock: houtals.count
    • Initial Value: 60 houtals
    • Inflows: houtals.incoming
    • Outflows: houtals.losses
    • Units: houtals
    • Documentation: Current stock accumulation of houtals.
  • Inflow: houtals.incoming
    • Equation: incoming_rate
    • Units: houtals/weeks
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Weekly incoming inflow to houtals.
  • Outflow: houtals.losses
    • Equation: count * loss_fraction
    • Units: houtals/weeks
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Proportional draining outflow of houtals.
  • Parameter: houtals.incoming_rate
    • Equation: 7
    • Units: houtals/weeks
    • Documentation: Constant weekly incoming rate of houtals.
  • Parameter: houtals.loss_fraction
    • Equation: 0.08
    • Units: 1/weeks
    • Documentation: Fractional weekly loss rate of houtals.

supportingInfo.explanation:
The quantitative Stock Flow Diagram (SFD) model has been created and validated according to your specifications.

Model Architecture and Modular Structure

The model consists of four dedicated modules corresponding to the four components, following the required naming conventions:

1. Module: outrances

  • Stock:
    • outrances.count: Initial value = 150 outrances
    • Inflows: outrances.replenishment
    • Outflows: outrances.losses, outrances.depletion
  • Flows:
    • outrances.replenishment: Equation = outrances.replenishment_rate (outrances/hour)
    • outrances.losses: Equation = outrances.count * outrances.loss_fraction (outrances/hour)
    • outrances.depletion: Equation = outrances.count * outrances.depletion_fraction (outrances/hour)
  • Parameters:
    • outrances.replenishment_rate: Equation = 20 outrances/hour
    • outrances.loss_fraction: Equation = 0.40 1/hour
    • outrances.depletion_fraction: Equation = 0.10 1/hour

2. Module: illigents

  • Stock:
    • illigents.count: Initial value = 30 illigents
    • Inflows: illigents.gain
    • Outflows: illigents.outgoing
  • Cross-Level Ghost:
    • illigents.outrances count: Ghost referencing outrances.count (outrances)
  • Flows:
    • illigents.gain: Equation = illigents.outrances_count * illigents.gain_fraction (illigents/hour)
    • illigents.outgoing: Equation = illigents.outgoing_rate (illigents/hour)
  • Parameters:
    • illigents.gain_fraction: Equation = 0.40 1/hour
    • illigents.outgoing_rate: Equation = 5 illigents/hour

3. Module: yelbs

  • Stock:
    • yelbs.count: Initial value = 65 yelbs
    • Inflows: yelbs.replenishment
    • Outflows: yelbs.reduction
  • Cross-Level Ghosts:
    • yelbs.outrances count: Ghost referencing outrances.count (outrances)
    • yelbs.trazes count: Ghost referencing trazes.count (trazes)
  • Flows:
    • yelbs.replenishment: Equation = yelbs.outrances_count * yelbs.replenishment_fraction (yelbs/hour)
    • yelbs.reduction: Equation = yelbs.trazes_count * yelbs.reduction_fraction (yelbs/hour)
  • Parameters:
    • yelbs.replenishment_fraction: Equation = 0.10 1/hour
    • yelbs.reduction_fraction: Equation = 0.12 1/hour

4. Module: trazes

  • Stock:
    • trazes.count: Initial value = 85 trazes
    • Inflows: trazes.gain
    • Outflows: trazes.losses
  • Flows:
    • trazes.gain: Equation = trazes.gain_rate (trazes/hour)
    • trazes.losses: Equation = trazes.count * trazes.loss_fraction (trazes/hour)
  • Parameters:
    • trazes.gain_rate: Equation = 15 trazes/hour
    • trazes.loss_fraction: Equation = 0.18 1/hour

Simulation Specifications

  • Start Time: 0
  • Stop Time: 24
  • Time Step (dt): 0.125
  • Time Units: hour
  • Integration Method: Euler

testParams.prompt:
Please give me a model which includes all causal relationships in the background information.

For readability, please create a module for each component, and use the following naming conventions:
- The module name should be the name of the object, pluralized if possible.
- Use component name "count" within the module to represent the quantity of the object.
- Flows can have any appropriate name.
- When creating a ghost, preserve the full name of the variable in the new module, replacing the period with a space where appropriate.

For example, for the object "whatamajig":
- Create module 'whatamajigs'
- Store count in 'whatamajigs.count'
- Ghosts should be named '[module].whatamajigs count'

additionalParameters.problemStatement:
I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

For readability, please create a module for each component, and use the following naming conventions:
- The module name should be the name of the object, pluralized if possible.
- Use component name "count" within the module to represent the quantity of the object.
- Flows can have any appropriate name.
- When creating a ghost, preserve the full name of the variable in the new module, replacing the period with a space where appropriate.

For example, for the object "whatamajig":
- Create module 'whatamajigs'

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: At the facility, we have on hand one hundred whatajigs. Every year, this inventory grows through incoming 5% growth relative to its current size. Simultaneously, each year the stock loses a constant three whatajigs.  Meanwhile, our records indicate two hundred balacks. Every year, this inventory is enhanced by 5% of the current whatajigs count. Simultaneously, each year the stock experiences losses of 3% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, the baseline inventory shows two hundred whoziewhats. Every year, this inventory gets replenished by 5% of the current balacks count. Simultaneously, each year the stock decreases by 3% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, there are initially twelve funkados. Every year, this inventory gets replenished by 5% of the current whoziewhats count. Simultaneously, each year the stock has outgoing 3% of whatever maxabizers are currently available.  Meanwhile, we start the period with eighty-eight maxabizers. Every year, this inventory receives new additions of 5% of the current funkados count. Simultaneously, each year the stock has outgoing 3% of whatever whoziewhats are currently available.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Architecture Overview

A modular System Dynamics Stock-Flow Diagram (SFD) has been constructed to represent all entities, interactions, and parameter rates specified in the background information. Each inventory component is encapsulated within its own dedicated module, utilizing standardized stock naming, explicit parameter formulation, and cross-module ghost variables.

Module Specifications

1. Module: whatajigs

  • Stock:
    • whatajigs.count: Initial value = 100 whatajigs. Inflows: [whatajigs.growth], Outflows: [whatajigs.loss]. Units: whatajigs.
  • Auxiliary Variables:
    • whatajigs.growth_fraction: 0.05 (5% annual growth rate). Units: 1/Years.
    • whatajigs.constant_loss_rate: 3 whatajigs/year. Units: whatajigs/Years.
  • Flows:
    • whatajigs.growth: Inflow defined as whatajigs.count * whatajigs.growth_fraction. Units: whatajigs/Years.
    • whatajigs.loss: Outflow defined as whatajigs.constant_loss_rate. Units: whatajigs/Years.

2. Module: balacks

  • Stock:
    • balacks.count: Initial value = 200 balacks. Inflows: [balacks.enhancement], Outflows: [balacks.losses]. Units: balacks.
  • Ghost Variable:
    • balacks.whatajigs count: Cross-level ghost referencing whatajigs.count. Units: whatajigs.
  • Auxiliary Variables:
    • balacks.enhancement_fraction: 0.05 (5% per year). Units: 1/Years.
    • balacks.loss_fraction: 0.03 (3% per year). Units: 1/Years.
  • Flows:
    • balacks.enhancement: Inflow defined as balacks.whatajigs_count * balacks.enhancement_fraction. Units: balacks/Years.
    • balacks.losses: Outflow defined as balacks.count * balacks.loss_fraction. Units: balacks/Years.

3. Module: whoziewhats

  • Stock:
    • whoziewhats.count: Initial value = 200 whoziewhats. Inflows: [whoziewhats.replenishment], Outflows: [whoziewhats.decrease]. Units: whoziewhats.
  • Ghost Variable:
    • whoziewhats.balacks count: Cross-level ghost referencing balacks.count. Units: balacks.
  • Auxiliary Variables:
    • whoziewhats.replenishment_fraction: 0.05 (5% per year). Units: 1/Years.
    • whoziewhats.decrease_fraction: 0.03 (3% per year). Units: 1/Years.
  • Flows:
    • whoziewhats.replenishment: Inflow defined as whoziewhats.balacks_count * whoziewhats.replenishment_fraction. Units: whoziewhats/Years.
    • whoziewhats.decrease: Outflow defined as whoziewhats.count * whoziewhats.decrease_fraction. Units: whoziewhats/Years.

4. Module: funkados

  • Stock:
    • funkados.count: Initial value = 12 funkados. Inflows: [funkados.replenishment], Outflows: [funkados.outgoing]. Units: funkados.
  • Ghost Variables:
    • funkados.whoziewhats count: Cross-level ghost referencing whoziewhats.count. Units: whoziewhats.
    • funkados.maxabizers count: Cross-level ghost referencing maxabizers.count. Units: maxabizers.
  • Auxiliary Variables:
    • funkados.replenishment_fraction: 0.05 (5% per year). Units: 1/Years.
    • funkados.outgoing_fraction: 0.03 (3% per year). Units: 1/Years.
  • Flows:
    • funkados.replenishment: Inflow defined as funkados.whoziewhats_count * funkados.replenishment_fraction. Units: funkados/Years.
    • funkados.outgoing: Outflow defined as funkados.maxabizers_count * funkados.outgoing_fraction. Units: funkados/Years.

5. Module: maxabizers

  • Stock:
    • maxabizers.count: Initial value = 88 maxabizers. Inflows: [maxabizers.additions], Outflows: [maxabizers.outgoing]. Units: maxabizers.
  • Ghost Variables:
    • maxabizers.funkados count: Cross-level ghost referencing funkados.count. Units: funkados.
    • maxabizers.whoziewhats count: Cross-level ghost referencing whoziewhats.count. Units: whoziewhats.
  • Auxiliary Variables:
    • maxabizers.addition_fraction: 0.05 (5% per year). Units: 1/Years.
    • maxabizers.outgoing_fraction: 0.03 (3% per year). Units: 1/Years.
  • Flows:
    • maxabizers.additions: Inflow defined as maxabizers.funkados_count * maxabizers.addition_fraction. Units: maxabizers/Years.
    • maxabizers.outgoing: Outflow defined as maxabizers.whoziewhats_count * maxabizers.outgoing_fraction. Units: maxabizers/Years.

Simulation Specifications

  • Start Time: 0
  • Stop Time: 50
  • Time Step (dt): 0.25
  • Time Units: Years
  • Integration Method: Euler

relationships.reasoning: A larger whatajigs inventory creates more annual growth.

relationships.reasoning: A higher growth fraction increases the annual growth flow.
relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in growth fraction causes an increase in growth rate.

relationships.reasoning: Growth adds to the total whatajigs count.

relationships.reasoning: Loss drains inventory from the whatajigs stock.
relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in the outflow decreases the stock.

relationships.reasoning: Losses deplete the balacks stock.

relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in replenishment fraction increases replenishment.

relationships.reasoning: Replenishment accumulates in whoziewhats inventory.
relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in replenishment increases whoziewhats count.

relationships.reasoning: More whoziewhats result in larger fractional decreases.

relationships.reasoning: Higher replenishment fraction increases replenishment rate.
relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in replenishment fraction increases replenishment.

relationships.reasoning: Replenishment increases funkados inventory.
relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in replenishment inflow increases funkados count.

relationships.reasoning: Maxabizers inventory drives the outgoing loss flow from funkados.
relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in maxabizers increases outgoing losses from funkados.

relationships.reasoning: Higher outgoing fraction increases outgoing rate.
relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in outgoing fraction increases outgoing rate.

relationships.reasoning: Outgoing losses reduce the funkados stock.
relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in outgoing outflow reduces funkados count.

relationships.reasoning: Funkados inventory drives addition flow into maxabizers.
relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in funkados increases additions to maxabizers.

relationships.reasoning: Higher addition fraction increases additions to maxabizers.
relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in addition fraction increases addition flow.

relationships.reasoning: Additions accumulate in maxabizers stock.
relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in additions inflow increases maxabizers count.

relationships.reasoning: Whoziewhats inventory drives the outgoing losses from maxabizers.

relationships.reasoning: Higher outgoing fraction increases outgoing flow from maxabizers.
relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in outgoing fraction increases outgoing rate.

relationships.reasoning: Outgoing flow depletes maxabizers inventory.
relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in outgoing flow reduces maxabizers count.
